correctness.rationale: The displayed normalized polynomial has Dirichlet energy exactly one and leading term of order m. Orthogonal Fourier expansion produces only three differences and exact constant Laurent coefficients through weighted degree six. A hand-reconstructible logarithmic expansion yields quartic coefficient (kappa-kappa_m)^2/m and, on that unique cancellation locus, sextic coefficient 2(lambda-lambda_m)^2/m+1/(24m). All omitted terms are analytic even powers and hence O(t^8) after degree six. Actual package checker verify.py was executed and reproduces both symbolic identities for general m; finite checks are supplemental, not substituted for the derivation. Positivity for all integer m>=1 follows directly from 1/(24m)>0.

value.rationale: The exact sharp functional has strict monomial equality yet a degenerate adjacent-mode Hessian. The unique quartic and subsequent uniquely optimized sextic cancellations are a structural Lyapunov–Schmidt phenomenon, not a generic Taylor exercise: they force any quantitative stability analysis to accommodate a sixth-order near-extremizing path and rule out quadratic and quartic Dirichlet-distance remainders. The universal positive coefficient 1/(24m) for every m in the canonical four-mode jet has a motivated precise invariant and can guide sharp stability conjectures. The finding does not assert a global sixth-order lower bound.
